tools.title: Azure DevOps
tools.summary: Boards, Repos, Pipelines, Test Plans and wikis from Microsoft.

servers.name: Azure DevOps MCP Server (remote)
servers.capabilities: Work items, repos and pull requests, pipelines, wikis, test plans, iterations and Advanced Security alerts; X-MCP-Toolsets and X-MCP-Readonly headers restrict tools.
servers.access: Work items, repos and pull requests, pipelines, wikis, test plans, iterations and Advanced Security alerts, read and write; Enterprise Live Migration tools (preview) are on by default.
servers.scopes: Microsoft Entra ID OAuth with an Entra-backed organization; Claude Code needs a custom app registration with the delegated permissions the team chooses and admin consent. Operations succeed only where both the OAuth scope and the user's Azure DevOps permissions allow.

read_only.how: The X-MCP-Readonly: true header restricts the server to read-only tools; X-MCP-Toolsets narrows the domains.

servers.name: Azure DevOps MCP Server (local)
servers.capabilities: Same domains as the remote server; -d flag loads only some domains (core, work-items...).

tools.notes: Remote server (preview, recommended) needs Microsoft Entra auth and an Entra-backed organization; Claude Desktop and Codex cannot use it, Claude Code and Cursor need a custom Entra app registration. Local server needs Node.js 20+, signs in with a Microsoft account or a PAT; new development goes to the remote server.

tools.title: Buildkite

servers.name: Buildkite remote MCP server
servers.capabilities: Pipelines, builds, jobs, logs and test data; read-only variant at /mcp/readonly, toolset scoping via /x/{toolset}.
servers.scopes: Buildkite permissions in the authorized organization. Consent: Sign in to Buildkite and approve access for the selected organization.

read_only.how: The endpoint https://mcp.buildkite.com/mcp/readonly exposes only read tools, over the resources of the authorized organization.

tools.notes: Headless agents with an API token use https://mcp.buildkite.com/direct (Authorization: Bearer, 50 requests/min per user). Docs say the server is under active development and hosted endpoints cannot be pinned to a version. A local Docker image (buildkite/mcp-server) also exists; its documented command passes the token as an argument, so it is not listed.

tools.title: CircleCI

servers.name: CircleCI MCP Server (hosted)
servers.capabilities: Pipeline and build status, failure logs and project data.
servers.access: Read operations described; no enforced read-only mode is recorded.

servers.name: CircleCI CLI MCP server
servers.capabilities: Same CircleCI tools, run locally from the CircleCI CLI.
servers.access: Read operations described; no enforced read-only mode is recorded.

tools.notes: Local CLI route: circleci auth login or CIRCLE_TOKEN, then circleci mcp claude|cursor|vscode enable. The old npx/Docker server (@circleci/mcp-server-circleci, CIRCLECI_TOKEN) is deprecated.

tools.title: Jenkins

servers.name: MCP Server plugin

settings.name: jenkins_host
settings.description: Jenkins: your jenkins host, without https://

servers.capabilities: Exposes Jenkins jobs, builds and logs as MCP tools and resources.
servers.access: Read or write, depending on the server configuration, the tools enabled or the consent given.

tools.notes: A plugin to install on the controller (version 0.228, needs Jenkins 2.541.3+). Auth is a Jenkins API token sent as HTTP Basic (username:token). Also serves SSE at /mcp-server/sse and a stateless endpoint at /mcp-server/stateless.
